styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Ribeira lanes, the cathedral and the Douro bridges.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Port cellars, francesinha and riverside tascas.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Serralves, São Bento tiles and street murals.

stays.why: On the river under the old houses. Walk to the bridge, boats and Port cellars. Noisy and hilly at night.
Flat, central and close to São Bento station, Bolhão market and metro. Best base for a first visit.
Quieter streets, galleries and cafés. Good value and a short walk or metro ride to the centre.
Modern hotels, the Casa da Música and Serralves nearby. Further out; use the metro or buses.

food: Try a francesinha (thick sandwich with sauce) at a local tasca. Portions are big; share if unsure.
Bacalhau (salt cod) comes many ways. Ask what is fresh that day.
Cross to Vila Nova de Gaia for Port cellar tours and tastings; book ahead in summer.
Bolhão market in Baixa is good for cheese, ham and a cheap lunch.
Sit down for grilled fish near the river, but check prices first. Expect around €12–25 a main.
more_time: Swap a city day for the Douro valley by train from São Bento; check times on the day.
Take a short coastal train or bus to Matosinhos for seafood and the beach.
Add a day trip to Guimarães or Braga by train for history and old streets.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Ribeira, the bridges, Port cellars and Serralves; add a night for a Douro or coastal day trip.

month_notes: January: cool and wet. Pack a rain jacket and plan indoor sights.
February: still cool with about 10 rain days. Bring layers.
March: mild but one of the wettest months. Keep plans flexible.
April: warmer and drier. Good for walking the old town.
May: pleasant days around 20°C. A strong month to visit.
June: warm and fairly dry. Long evenings by the river.
July: warmest and driest. Book hotels and cellar tours early.
August: hot and dry, and busy with visitors. Go early or late in the day.
September: still warm and drier than autumn. Good value.
October: rain returns, about 13 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
November: wet and cooler. Fewer crowds, lower prices.
December: cool and wet with festive lights in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Atlantic climate: wet from October to March, warm and dry in July and August.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 20–25°C and few rain days, especially July and August.

items.title: Wettest months: October to March
items.text: Around 12–14 rain days a month. Bring a rain jacket and waterproof shoes.

items.title: Mild winters
items.text: January highs near 13°C and lows near 7°C. Rarely freezing, but damp and chilly.

items.title: Warm summers, not extreme
items.text: July and August peak around 24–25°C. Comfortable for walking, but the hills are steep.

items.title: Rain can come any month
items.text: Even summer has a few wet days. A small umbrella is worth packing.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket and comfortable shoes for cobbled hills. Add sunglasses and a hat for summer.

transit.best: Walk in the centre and use the metro for longer hops; use Uber or Bolt for the airport.

modes.text: Line E links the airport to the centre. Validate your Andante card before boarding.
STCP buses cover the city. Night bus 3M runs to the airport hourly.
Uber and Bolt work well. Airport rides cost about €10–25.
Driving is chaotic: narrow hilly streets and hard parking. Best avoided.
The best way around the centre, though it is hilly.
Douro river boats and the Leixões harbour serve cruise and tour trips.
